name: Punk
blurb: Three-chord punk: a downstroke power-chord wall on straight 8ths, a flat-out kick-and-snare drive with zero ghost notes, and a root-locked pick bass.

flavors.label: Three Chords
flavors.blurb: I-IV-V, all downstrokes, nothing held longer than a bar -- 1977 with the amp on ten.

flavors.label: Pop-Punk
flavors.blurb: The Axis and its vi rotation played bright and dead tight -- built for a chorus you can shout.

flavors.label: Hardcore Blast
flavors.blurb: Two chords oscillating flat out, pushed ahead of the click and barely hanging on.

flavors.label: Half-Time Mosh
flavors.blurb: Drop to half speed and slam two chords -- the breakdown everyone waits for.

flavors.label: Post-Punk Chime
flavors.blurb: Clean, ringing minor chords instead of a distorted wall -- cold, spare and hypnotic.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: Punk harmony is three chords and the truth: I-IV-V, the I-V-vi-IV axis and its vi-IV-I-V rotation, or a minor i-bVII-bVI drive. One chord per bar, all downstrokes, root-position power shapes. Never write sevenths, extensions or borrowed chords -- they sound instantly wrong. Two-chord oscillations and one-chord blasts are legitimate whole songs.
